command: node scripts/scorecard-recovery-sim.js --name=step-25 --note=BUG FIX (round 4): irt.js packed an answer's context with pace and prior_correct under the same key ('pc'), so since step 17 every stored context lost its earlier-right count and the forgetting model read nc as the pace flag (0 or 1) and nw as nearly every earlier attempt. Each field now has its own key, checked at load. decay_rate / retention / retrieval r 0.49 -> 0.54 at 100 levels (standing r 0.49 -> 0.54); every other number unchanged. (Memory-kind stats still steer no lesson: step 22's over-confidence finding was made with the corrupted counts and is worth re-measuring, but a recall-recap directive is something the research says to bake into every lesson anyway.)

definitions.false_directive: a lesson directive (translate.directives, use L) whose side contradicts the side of 50 the true value is on
definitions.severe_false_directive: a directive whose true value is past the OPPOSITE edge (e.g. "high" fired, truth <= 30)
definitions.unmeasured_directive: a directive on a stat that received less behavioural + feedback-tap + experiment weight than the confidence gate needs (1.07); i.e. the questionnaire and the model read carried it
definitions.recall: of learners whose true value is past an edge with directive text on that side, the share with that directive
definitions.mae_if_always_50: the error of a card that never moves: the bar a stat has to beat to have learned anything
